q: In the context of random dynamical systems, the Furstenberg theorem on random matrix products states that for i.i.d. matrices A₁, A₂, … chosen from a distribution μ on GL(d,ℝ) satisfying irreducibility and strong irreducibility:
opts: The matrix products Aₙ…A₁ are bounded
The Lyapunov exponent λ = lim_{n→∞} (1/n) log||Aₙ…A₁|| > −∞ exists and λ > −∞ a.s.
The products converge to a fixed matrix
The products have zero Lyapunov exponent
exp: Furstenberg's theorem: under irreducibility + strong irreducibility, the top Lyapunov exponent λ₁ is simple and positive (the distribution is not supported on compact groups). This implies the products grow exponentially—relevant for products of transfer matrices in disordered systems.
